recurringPatterns.pattern: Symmetrical epistemic hedge: 'It can... It cannot' adjacent sentences
instances: A skull with a fracture can tell us that a force struck it... It does not reveal whether the attackers distinguished among them.
A court register may be strong evidence that a dispute was heard and weak evidence that most disputes reached court.

recurringPatterns.pattern: Every section closes on a concrete object or micro-image standing in for the argument
instances: The reed marker lies beside the pit, bent but unbroken.
The enumerator's ink dried beside a name that would outlast the visit.

recurringPatterns.pattern: The 'what evidence would settle this?' interlude as a near-identical subsection in several chapters
instances: What would allow us to decide whether the apparent decline of violence...
What evidence would settle the question more securely? A comparison would need local records...

recurringPatterns.pattern: Steelman-then-narrow: strongest rival explanation stated, conceded in part, reduced to 'a narrower claim'
instances: The strongest objection to this argument is that formal law marked a broad humanitarian advance.
The strongest rival explanation begins with the crowd.

recurringPatterns.pattern: Paragraph-initial 'Nor' / 'Yet' pivots as the default connective for qualification
instances: Nor does the cycle prove that all dynasties must decline in the same way.
Yet skepticism becomes too strong when it treats the formula as empty.

summary: Disciplined synthesis with a genuine thesis and well-chosen cases; dominant flaw is structural repetition (can/cannot hedge, steelman-then-narrow, closing image, what-would-settle interlude); set pieces lapse into beat-by-beat description; cut a fifth and vary paragraph shape.
